items.title: Mississauga Turns to Licence Plate Cameras to Catch Drivers Who Speed Off From School Zones
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga's parking enforcement division began using Licence Plate Recognition technology on Oct. 1 to crack down on drivers who park illegally in school zones and drive off before an officer can reach their vehicle. The cameras scan license plates of illegally parked cars, and the city then mails infraction notices directly to the registered vehicle owner rather than relying on a ticket placed on the windshield. City officials say the system is meant to help in spots where a physical notice isn't practical, such as school zones and time-limited parking areas, though officers will keep placing tickets by hand when that's still workable. The technology is rolling out first in school zones to improve road safety and traffic flow around schools, with the city planning to expand it to additional locations in 2027. The move follows a round of parking fine increases across Mississauga that took effect in April 2025, when the penalty for illegally stopping in a school zone jumped to $145 from $65. City officials frame the cameras as a way to both improve safety for enforcement staff and make ticket delivery more consistent. The rollout is one of several changes introduced this month within the city's parking enforcement division.

items.title: New Canadian Play 'the joshis' Brings Diwali-Set Family Drama to Mississauga Stage This October
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga, SAWITRI Theatre Group has teamed up with Very Serious Theatre Company to stage the joshis, a new Canadian play by Max Kingsbury, running Oct. 22 to 30 at AN1 Studios in Mississauga. The story follows a family gathered to celebrate the festival of lights, with the celebration taking a dramatic turn that changes their lives. The production is directed by Devansh Shah and Raina Desai and carries a content warning for strong language, with a recommended minimum age of 14. Jasmine Sawant, SAWITRI's founder and artistic co-director, says the company is redefining how culturally rooted stories can move, challenge and unite contemporary audiences. Founded in 2003 and based in Mississauga, SAWITRI is an award-winning not-for-profit that has produced more than 93 works, including 23 full-length plays across English, Marathi, Gujarati and Hindi. The company also runs the Mississauga Multilingual Fringe Festival, which it describes as the only multilingual fringe festival in North America. SAWITRI's operations receive partial funding from the City of Mississauga and the Ontario Arts Council.

items.title: MiWay Marks National Seniors Day by Touting Free Rides for Mississauga's Fastest-Growing Age Group
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, MiWay is marking National Seniors Day on Oct. 1 by highlighting how many older residents now rely on transit to stay active and independent. The city says seniors are one of Mississauga's fastest-growing populations, with forecasts suggesting the number of residents 65 and older could grow by 45 per cent by 2051. MiWay already ranks among the largest transit systems in Ontario, running nearly 70 routes across more than 3,000 stops and logging 52 million boardings in 2025. Riders 65 and older can travel free by setting their PRESTO card to the senior fare type, which requires visiting a customer service outlet and showing proof of age, since a card left on the default setting is charged the regular adult fare. City officials say the free fare, accessible buses and direct routes help seniors avoid the stress of driving, parking and traffic while getting to shopping, medical appointments and recreation closer to home. The city frames the ridership data as evidence that transit is becoming a bigger part of how Mississauga's seniors stay connected to their community.

items.title: Firefighters' Union Backs Crombie's Push to Reclaim Mayor's Chair From Parrish
items.summary: According to CityNews, the Mississauga Fire Fighters Association has endorsed Bonnie Crombie in her bid to become mayor again. The union says Crombie's community safety plan would strengthen emergency services, speed up 911 response times and expand investment in mental-health support. Association president Chris Varcoe said firefighters know that keeping a community safe takes leadership, preparation and a willingness to listen to the people on the front lines. Varcoe added that the group trusts Crombie to work with its members and make the safety of Mississauga families a priority. Crombie previously served as mayor from 2014 to 2024 before stepping down to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. She resigned as party leader earlier this year after the Liberals finished third in the 2025 Ontario election and she failed to win a seat herself, despite receiving 57 per cent support in a subsequent leadership review. Crombie is now looking to return to Mississauga's top job and will face off against incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish in the race.

items.title: Peel Police Identify Suspect Vehicle as 1999-2005 Chevrolet Silverado in Fatal Dundas Street Hit-and-Run
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, investigators have identified the type of vehicle involved in Tuesday evening's fatal hit-and-run on Dundas Street West in Mississauga. Police say a pedestrian was crossing in a crosswalk when a dark-coloured pickup truck travelling south on Winston Churchill Boulevard turned west onto Dundas Street West and struck him, then fled the scene without stopping. Officers, firefighters and paramedics arrived and attempted life-saving measures, but the man was pronounced dead at the scene. He has been described only as a man in his 60s, and police have not released his name. On Wednesday, Const. Tyler Bell-Morena told reporters that investigators have now narrowed down the suspect vehicle to a 1999 to 2005 model year Chevrolet Silverado 500 series pickup truck, two-tone in colour. Police released surveillance video showing the moments leading up to the collision in hopes the footage will help the public identify the driver. Investigators say they believe it is only a matter of time before the person responsible is found and are urging anyone with information to come forward.

items.title: 500,000 Jobs Already Surround Pearson Airport as Ottawa Weighs a Private Operator
items.summary: According to a column published by Insauga, the federal government's plan to install a private operator at Toronto Pearson International Airport could mean far more for Mississauga than higher fees or extra noise. The piece, written by a former Greater Toronto Airports Authority employee, argues that Pearson's real asset is its location, since the airport sits on 1,867 hectares of federal land at the centre of Canada's second-largest employment zone. Citing a 2025 Deloitte study prepared for the GTAA, the column notes that zone already supports more than 500,000 jobs, many of them in Mississauga, with access to highways 401, 427, 409 and 407 as well as the Kitchener GO line and the UP Express. The author suggests a new ownership model could eventually turn parts of the airport lands into an urban hub resembling the airport cities built in parts of Asia and Europe. Pearson is currently run by the GTAA, which leases the federal land and operates its buildings and runways to fund upkeep and growth. The column frames Prime Minister Mark Carney's privatization plan as a shift in who controls that existing model rather than an entirely new concept, and argues the underlying economics make the idea worth watching closely.

items.title: Raptors Star Scottie Barnes Joins Ribbon-Cutting for New Athletic Wing at Mississauga's TFS Campus
items.summary: According to Insauga, Toronto French School's West Campus in Lakeview marked the start of the new school year with a ribbon-cutting for a new 12,600-square-foot athletic and arts expansion. TFS is known as Canada's first French immersion school and describes itself as the country's only bilingual, full continuum IB World School. The new space, funded in part by contributions from parents, alumni and staff, includes a junior regulation-sized gymnasium called Gymnase Kaneff, a viewing gallery overlooking it known as Galerie Bechara, an upgraded school entrance and renovated classrooms. It also adds a design studio equipped for students to work on engineering, robotics and other hands-on problem solving. Toronto Raptors forward Scottie Barnes attended the grand opening, taking part in a question-and-answer session with students before leading them through basketball drills. The school plans to hold a series of open houses and guided tours over the coming months so families can see the new centre firsthand. TFS says the expansion is meant to help students build confidence, leadership and teamwork skills while serving the broader Mississauga community for years to come.

items.title: Height Lowered to 37 Storeys as Ontario Tribunal Settles Erin Mills Mall Redevelopment Fight
items.summary: According to Insauga, a nine-tower redevelopment of the Erin Mills Town Centre property has won approval through a settlement at the Ontario Land Tribunal. The plan covers the mall's northwest quadrant at 5100 Erin Mills Parkway, where existing restaurants and shops would be demolished to make way for the project. The original proposal called for towers ranging from 20 to 44 storeys and totalling 3,162 units, a scale that drew opposition from residents at public meetings held in 2025. Neighbours raised concerns about building heights, a lack of affordable and rental units, and the loss of existing retail space in the area. The property owner appealed to the tribunal after arguing that city council had failed to act on the official plan amendment and rezoning applications, and the tribunal holds the authority to override municipal decisions in such cases. Mississauga and the developer ultimately reached a settlement, approved by the tribunal last week, that trims the maximum height to 37 storeys while keeping nine towers in the plan. The revised proposal also adds a public park, an urban plaza and a new pedestrian and road network, with construction expected to proceed in phases.
